input: Interview three interior designers before committing

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The size and type of the design project (full home, single room, renovation vs. new décor) determines what skills and experience to screen for in the interviews.
Knowing whether the user already has specific designers in mind or needs to find candidates from scratch changes whether the first step is sourcing or scheduling.
Whether the interviews are in-person, virtual, or at the project site affects logistics and how designers will assess the space.
The budget range for the design project is the single most important filter for which designers are even worth interviewing.
The design style or aesthetic the user wants (minimalist, maximalist, Scandinavian, etc.) determines what to look for in a designer's portfolio.
Understanding what factors will drive the final hiring decision (personality fit, price, portfolio, process) shapes what questions to ask in each interview.
The deadline by which the user needs to hire someone determines how urgently the interviews need to be scheduled and how much sourcing time is available.

gold.taskTitle: Interview three interior designers before hiring
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to interview at least three interior designers and evaluate them before making a hiring decision for a design project.

questions.title: What space or project is being designed?
questions.description: Identify the scope of the design project — e.g., a single room, a full home, a renovation, or a new build — so interviews can be tailored to relevant experience.

questions.title: Do you have candidates in mind, or start from scratch?
questions.description: Determine whether the user already has designers to contact or needs to research and source candidates first.

questions.title: Will interviews be in-person, virtual, or on-site?
questions.description: Clarify the intended format of the interviews to plan scheduling and logistics appropriately.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this design project?
questions.description: Establish a budget range so that only designers whose fees are aligned are shortlisted and interviewed.

questions.title: What design style or aesthetic are you aiming for?
questions.description: Understand the user's visual and stylistic preferences so portfolio review criteria can be defined before the interviews.

questions.title: What will matter most when choosing the final designer?
questions.description: Identify the top decision factors — such as price, portfolio, communication style, or process — to build a focused interview scorecard.

questions.title: By when do you need to have someone hired?
questions.description: Establish the hiring deadline to determine how quickly interviews need to be scheduled and how much time is available for sourcing.
